limits: Client-observed streams, not isolated provider computation or semantic reasoning.
Parent and child windows overlap and are nonadditive.
Child windows start at recorded thread creation and end at task completion when observed, otherwise the capture boundary.
Incomplete output lacks a completed interval; response usage may straddle boundaries.
First stream event is used with the persisted item completion; stderr does not expose the desktop logger event labels.
Raw logs and capabilities remain private; this output includes metadata only.
Client stream intervals are not provider compute time or pure semantic reasoning.
Reading inputs can include implicit comparison before the timed gate.
The prior desktop trial and this CLI/MCP trial have different transport and paging overhead; this is not a controlled transport-only A/B.
Same model, effort, source JSON values and compact-plan scope; generated plans can differ.
Nested phase windows overlap; usage is attributed by response completion, with cached/reasoning counters being subsets.
Service-call observer wraps existing production methods and records metadata; HTTP timing includes its small observation overhead.
This ends at a compact plan, excluding full UX assembly, independent review and repairs.
